title: NVMe (cold-tier storage)
subtitle: The broker's cold tier is NVMe: billions of queued tokens survive a restart in shape-pure order.

stats.label: shape switches while draining one backlog
NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs fed from one cold tier

lede: Inference Fabric put a broker between producers that submit millions of tokenised tasks and walk away, and GPU consumers that pull work as fast as they can process it. The two sides run at different speeds for hours. Producers burst far ahead of the GPUs, and the GPUs must never wait on a producer. A backlog of billions of tokens does not fit in memory, and losing it on a restart would mean regenerating hours of queued work. I gave the broker a cold tier on local NVMe: an append-only store of memory-mapped segments, with only the hot working set in RAM, so disk sets the backlog's size.
quote: I treat local NVMe as a deliberate tier in a throughput system, laid out for the way the consumer reads.
evidence: NVMe as a storage tier for GPU pipelines: a broker cold tier of append-only, memory-mapped segments on local NVMe that keeps a backlog of billions of queued tokens across restarts.
Message broker and queue design: work grouped by token shape before it reaches disk, so one backlog drained across two NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs with 0 shape switches and 0.42% padding waste.
Distributed systems correctness: an item counted done only when its result was delivered and acknowledged, after which 12.3B tokens received matched 12.3B routed.
author: Corey James
